      "value": "Initially, when a +40 V gate voltage is applied, electrons will tunnel through β-Ga2O3 and transfer to the graphene FG. What’s more, when a −40 V gate voltage is used to erase, the electrons in graphene will be transferred to the MoS2 channel, thereby forcing the MoS2 channel into an on-state. Thus, the MoS2/β-Ga2O3/MLG FG memory is capable of realizing two-level non-volatile storage by electrostatic control.",

    {
      "value": "In dark conditions, the β-Ga2O3 functions as a high-κ dielectric layer with minimal leakage current, allowing for precise regulation of the channel’s carrier density and surface potential through the application of Vcg.       "value": "Upon application of an electrical pulse with a voltage of −30 V for 0.01 s, electrons initially tunnel through β-Ga2O3 and migrate to the MoS2 channel, completing the erasing operation. Subsequently, following the removal of the gate voltage, a significant accumulation of holes occurs in the graphene, which the MoS2 channel interprets as a positive gate voltage, thereby maintaining an on-state. Subsequently, DUV light (254 nm) with pulse widths of 1 s is used for programming, which could excite electrons from the valence bands of both β-Ga2O3 and MoS2, leading to the generation of electron-hole pairs. However, only the carriers originating from β-Ga2O3 are capable of transiting into either channel or FG. Within the graphene FG, the electrons will be neutralized with holes, effectively reducing the gate voltage, whereas in the MoS2 channel, the holes will recombine with the electrons, reducing the lifetime of the majority carriers.
